lineage_induction_events.mechanistic_diagnosis: The new witness has positive accumulated past overstress and a banding index below 0.50, even though its present stress is below the critical threshold. Past damage activates crystallization through tanh(D_cryst), adding a stress-dependent exponential transient and replacing linear terminal flow with log(1+t). Because log(1+t) has unit slope at t=0, the initial-rate formula retains the full modified drift coefficient. Both physical calibration parents change predictions through calibrated past and hold stresses, which feed the memory gaps, damage activation, and crystallization terms. Auxiliary chamber telemetry and the unrelated sentinel do not enter the prediction equations. The guards separate both tested witnesses.

The jammed-slip witness has zero past exceedance but a shear-banding index of 0.82, so the old base guard misroutes it. Above 0.50, shear banding selects the saturating terminal-flow law with signed square-root slip and gap-difference coupling. Gate on banding first, then use past exceedance to distinguish the two lower-banding branches. This gives exactly one match for each tested witness. Both physical calibration parents can change strain and initial-rate predictions through the calibrated stress history and terminal hold; auxiliary telemetry and the sentinel task have no such path. Separately, the visible solver reads the archive for every two-point sweep with distinct commands, even when both points are clean.

Positive accumulated past overstress, not present hold-stress exceedance, activates strain crystallization when the shear-banding index is at most 0.50. The new branch replaces linear terminal flow with a logarithmic plateau and adds damage-gated corrections to the transient and terminal amplitudes. At zero accumulated damage those corrections vanish. Both physical calibration parents affect the prediction through calibrated stress history and hold stress; auxiliary telemetry and the unrelated sentinel do not.

When the shear-banding index exceeds 0.50, terminal flow follows the saturating kernel t/(1+0.85t). Its coefficient includes signed square-root slip, and a separate transient couples the two memory gaps. The saturating kernel still has unit slope at t=0. Both physical calibration parents affect the stress history and hold stress, which determine the memory gaps and slip; auxiliary telemetry and the unrelated sentinel do not enter the predictions. Component IDs below are descriptive because no canonical component IDs were supplied.

The new witness activates strain crystallization through positive accumulated past stress damage in the low-banding regime, even though the present stress is below the critical threshold. Crystallization replaces linear terminal flow with log(1+t) and adds activation-dependent transient and terminal terms. The logarithmic basis retains unit slope at t=0, but the added terms change the predicted initial rate. Both physical calibration parents can change predictions through the calibrated stress history and hold stress; auxiliary telemetry and the unrelated sentinel cannot. The guards separate the supplied witnesses; the existing guard does not establish coverage for untested high-banding cases.

The old C0 guard admits the jammed-slip witness because its past-series exceedance integral is zero. Jammed slip instead activates when the shear-banding index exceeds 0.50, independently of past exceedance. The new solver retains the two-branch hereditary memory and uses a saturating terminal-flow kernel with signed square-root slip and a gap-difference transient. Both physical calibration parents affect the calibrated stress history and hold stress, and thus the predicted strain and initial rate. Auxiliary chamber telemetry and the unrelated sentinel are uncoupled.
